$comment: FROZEN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT LIST FOR RULE 8 (GOV-H, 2026-11-01).
WHY A FREEZE LIST IS NECESSARY, NOT A CONVENIENCE. Rule 8 finds 7 pre-existing
instances of the FK/NOT NULL/CHECK contradiction in migrations already on
origin/main. Every one of those files is at or below the attested applied
boundary 20270111000003, which rule 6 declares IMMUTABLE. A gate that failed
on files another rule forbids editing could never be satisfied, so it would be
switched off — and a gate that is off catches nothing. Freezing the known set
is what lets the rule be a real, enforced gate for every NEW migration, which
is the same bargain scripts/migrations/historical-baseline.txt already makes.
THIS LIST IS NOT A DISMISSAL. Each entry is reported as a known open item on
every run and names its owner. Remediation is forward-only: a NEW migration
above the boundary that fixes the shape. Nobody edits the listed file.
WHAT IT PROVES. Entry 7 is
20270105000000_pi_prospect_problem_observations.sql — the migration that
INTRODUCED DEFECT-008. Rule 8 flags it from the migration text alone, with no
database, in the one required status check on main. Had this rule existed when
that migration was authored, the defect would have failed the PR instead of
reaching production. Entries 3, 4 and 6 are the three sibling defects this
programme is remediating now (Agents C, D and B), found the same way.
Removing an entry is only correct once a forward migration has fixed the shape
AND the catalog detector (scripts/ci/check-actor-fk-compatibility.js --db)
confirms it on a replayed schema.
KEY FORMAT: '<migration file>:<column>' — the line number is deliberately NOT
part of the key, so an unrelated edit elsewhere in a file cannot silently
un-freeze or re-freeze an entry.

known.detail: The CHECK is DISJUNCTIVE: person_id IS NOT NULL OR (target_normalized IS NOT NULL AND length(btrim(target_normalized)) > 0). A row whose target_normalized is set survives person_id going NULL, and line 22 of the migration shows ON DELETE SET NULL (person_id) was a deliberate choice. But a row with person_id set and target_normalized blank DOES fail on delete. Rule 8 cannot distinguish a disjunctive fallback from a conjunctive requirement and should not pretend to; the right resolution is a reviewed '-- set-null-ok: <reason>' on a forward migration, or a NOT-blank guarantee for target_normalized.

$comment_not_modelled: A FOURTH ARMING MECHANISM THIS DETECTOR CANNOT SEE.
A SET NULL referential action IS an UPDATE, and a CASCADE IS a DELETE. So a
BEFORE UPDATE / BEFORE DELETE trigger whose body can RAISE or RETURN NULL
refuses the referential action itself and aborts the parent delete with P0001
or 42501. That is a third way a column 'cannot hold NULL' — and it is invisible
to this detector, which models only declared nullability and CHECK constraints.
Reporting such an FK as clean would be the worst thing this gate could do, so
the keys are named here instead.
NOT RE-DERIVED. These verdicts are AGENT F's, from a guard-body analysis on
w6_a6 (their reconcile_60.json). They are consumed here as evidence, with
attribution, and must be reconciled at programme consolidation rather than
maintained independently by this track.
WHY A TRIGGER-AWARE RULE IS DELIBERATELY NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE. Gating on the
PRESENCE of a BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE guard over-counts fivefold: Agent A's
catalog census of that shape returns 60 on this schema, of which only 12 are
armed. 46 of the other 48 sit under a guard whose entire body is
'NEW.updated_at := NOW(); RETURN NEW;' — no RAISE, no RETURN NULL — so it
cannot refuse anything. The deciding predicate is the guard BODY (does it RAISE,
or RETURN NULL), never the trigger's presence and never its name: Agent F's
first pass filtered on a name regex before reading any body and correctly
called that 'a heuristic dressed as a filter'. A body analyser belongs in one
place, and that place is Agent F's track, not a second copy here.
OF THESE 12, EXACTLY ONE (prospect_lifecycle_transitions.actor_user_id) IS ALSO
FOUND BY THIS DETECTOR — through its CHECK constraint, not its trigger. The
other 11 this detector reports as clean, and they are NOT.
`verdict` is Agent F's: BLOCKS = the guard refuses the action outright;
CONDITIONAL = it refuses for some rows.
